CSRs according to privilege level as shown in <<csrrwpriv>>. [#norm:Zicsr_rw]#The top two bits (csr[11:10]) indicate whether the register is read/write (`00`,`01`, or `10`) or read-only (`11`).#
[#norm:Zicsr_access]#The next two bits (csr[9:8]) encode the lowest privilege level that can access the CSR, with the pattern `10` representing hypervisor CSRs.#

[#norm:Zicsr_illegal_acc]#Attempts to write a read-only CSR address raise illegal-instruction exceptions.#
[#norm:Zicsr_write_ro]#A read/write register might also contain some bits that are
read-only, in which case writes to the read-only bits are ignored.#

[#norm:Zicsr_nonexistent_rsv]#Instructions that access a non-existent CSR address are reserved.#

<<csrrwpriv>> also indicates the convention to

[#norm:mvendorid_always_rd]#This register must be readable in any implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to
indicate the field is not implemented or that this is a non-commercial implementation.#

[#norm:marchid_always_rd]#This register must be readable in any
implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate the field is not implemented.#
The combination of csr:mvendorid[] and csr:marchid[] should uniquely identify the type of hart microarchitecture that is implemented.

[#norm:mimpid_always_rd]#This register must be readable in any
implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate that the field is not implemented.#
The Implementation value should reflect the design of the RISC-V processor itself and not any surrounding system.

following decreasing priority order: MEI, MSI, MTI, SEI, SSI, STI, LCOFI.#
